items.stem: An executive judges a past decision as bad purely because it lost money. What is the flaw in this reasoning?

options.text: It conflates decision quality with outcome, ignoring the role of uncertainty and luck
options.rationale: Correct: a sound decision can still have a poor outcome under uncertainty.

options.text: Losing money always means the decision was good
options.rationale: The opposite claim is equally flawed.

options.text: Outcomes are the only valid measure of decisions
options.rationale: Outcomes alone ignore process quality and luck.

options.text: Decision quality cannot be assessed at all
options.rationale: It can, by examining the process and information at the time.

items.explanation: Correct: a sound decision can still have a poor outcome under uncertainty.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO techniques most directly counter overconfidence in an executive forecast? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reference-class forecasting using base rates from similar cases
options.rationale: Correct: base rates anchor estimates in real comparable outcomes.

options.text: Running a pre-mortem imagining the decision has failed
options.rationale: Correct: pre-mortems surface overlooked failure modes.

options.text: Asking the most confident person to decide alone
Removing all dissent to decide faster
Rounding the forecast to a single optimistic number
options.rationale: A single optimistic point ignores uncertainty.

items.explanation: Correct: base rates anchor estimates in real comparable outcomes.

items.stem: A reversible, low-stakes decision has stalled for weeks awaiting more analysis. What is the best executive guidance?

options.text: Decide quickly and adjust later, reserving deep analysis for high-stakes irreversible choices
options.rationale: Correct: reversible low-stakes decisions reward speed and learning over exhaustive analysis.

options.text: Commission a full analysis regardless of stakes
Escalate every such decision to the CEO
options.rationale: Escalation is unnecessary for low-stakes reversible calls.
Certainty is rarely available and not required here.

items.explanation: Correct: reversible low-stakes decisions reward speed and learning over exhaustive analysis.
